newsitem.title: USA: Genzyme sees strong response to Seprafilm.
newsitem.headline: Genzyme sees strong response to Seprafilm.

text.p: Genzyme Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Henri Termeer said he is "very encouraged" by the reception of Seprafilm, its product to prevent surgical adhesions, which won FDA approval last August and was commercialized in October.
In the first three months of commercialization, he said the product was ordered by 347 U.S. hospitals, and that of those, 29 percent have reordered it so far.
Speaking at the Hambrecht and Quist Healthcare Conference here, Termeer said that revenues from its pharmaceutical division, which rose sharply during 1996, are expected to be flat in 1997.
"We would expect to see (that unit's) sales next year between $40 million and $45 million," Termeer said. He estimated 1996 sales would reach $43 million, up from $30 million in 1995.
But, he said, sales of melatonin, the non-prescription, all-natural sleeping drug, which rose rapidly early this year, have since plateaued.
"It was very big in the first quarter, but unfortunately has been flat since then," he said.
